boundary_decisions.rationale: Pipeline names a graph and operating arrangement, not one semantic or adoption boundary.
A suite may package movement products but cannot re-own their state, authority or failure semantics.
Connection lifecycle and revocation are coherent, but independent exit and cross-runtime conformance evidence remain incomplete.
CDC has independent source-log state, recovery, operation and substitution boundaries.
Managed ingestion owns independent declarations, delivery state, SLO, recovery and source-to-target exit.
Orchestration owns workflow/run/attempt state and is replaceable without redefining task semantics.
Stateful dataflow has independent plan, state, time, checkpoint, recovery and runtime boundaries.
The build engine has a coherent manifest/materialization promise, but often remains bundled with warehouse execution and orchestration.
Durable event transport has independent users, protocol, state, SLO, cost and exit from transformation engines.
Operational activation has independent destination mappings, business-effect authority, recovery and destination-side exit.
A vendor connector implements a typed connection/capture/delivery offer; vendor naming does not create product semantics.
End-to-end exactly-once requires source replay, state recovery and sink transaction/idempotency evidence; an engine checkpoint mode alone is insufficient.
Movement products emit run evidence but lineage owns the observed derivation model and limitations.
Pipeline is horizontal composition; industry vocabulary, source mappings, rules and decision cases belong in solution packs.
An agent or model may propose mappings or recovery actions but does not create pipeline semantics, source authority or an executed effect.

negative_tests.input_claim: Every data pipeline is one product.
The data integration suite owns every cursor, checkpoint and task state.
Every branded connector or plugin is a sovereign product.
A database log cursor, broker offset and delivery cursor are interchangeable integers.
A successful orchestrator task proves records were committed exactly once.
An exactly-once engine checkpoint proves exactly-once external effects.
The orchestrator may redefine the semantic meaning of a task result.
A broker or CloudEvents envelope owns the business meaning of its payload.
An OpenLineage dependency event proves causal influence.
A successful dbt build proves universal data quality.
The transformation engine may infer business grain from a convenient unique key.
A model row authorizes an update to a CRM or operational system.
Copying source records transfers source-system business authority to ingestion.
ETL versus ELT ordering determines product boundaries.
A generic pipeline supplies banking, healthcare, sports or energy language and rules.
Adding an LLM mapping assistant or agent creates new pipeline semantics or effect authority.

ownership.invariant: A declaration identifies desired access and configuration, never a credential value or source grant.
A binding names exact source occurrence, connector/profile and scoped credential reference.
A source-native cursor is not a broker offset, workflow logical date or destination checkpoint.
A snapshot cut records the source visibility boundary and stitching relation to live changes.
A captured change preserves source operation, identity, before/after availability and cursor evidence.
Delivery progress records acknowledged source-to-target work and is distinct from source and broker cursors.
A receipt names input cut, sink effect profile and acknowledged target state; it is not a quality certificate.
A workflow orders tasks and conditions but cannot redefine a task's semantic result.
A run is one workflow-definition edition over a logical interval and trigger, distinct from task attempts.
Retries create distinct attempts; success does not establish data correctness or idempotent effects.
A logical graph is provider-neutral and distinct from runner plans and workflow task graphs.
Operator state is versioned against operator identity, partitioning and serializer compatibility.
A watermark is a progress assertion with lateness assumptions, not wall-clock time or completeness proof.
A checkpoint binds operator state and source positions; it does not alone prove external exactly-once effects.
A manifest identifies parsed resource definitions and dependencies for an exact project edition.
Materialization declares desired target behavior and must be lowered against exact adapter capabilities.
A build receipt distinguishes selected, executed, passed, failed and skipped resources.
A transport offset locates broker log progress and is never substituted for a source transaction cursor.
Retention bounds broker replay availability and cannot imply source-system history retention.
Mapping binds governed analytical identity to an exact destination object and field edition.
An insert/update/upsert/delete proposal requires separate purpose and destination authority before execution.
A destination receipt records observed API effect outcome without asserting downstream business success.
Movement preserves or translates a source fact but cannot issue it.
Run evidence supports observed derivation only within explicit facet and collection limits.
The envelope owner governs provider-neutral event metadata, not payload truth, log position, delivery or business acceptance.
The retained-log owner governs log identity, epoch, partition, position and retained ranges, not source cursors or consumer progress.
The consumer-group owner governs assignment-fenced transport progress, not source capture, operator checkpoints or business effects.
